deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. The previous page develops sine- and cosine-like elliptic functions in products whose factors contain e^{(k/2)·π/√3}. It ends with the numerator (Zähler) as a sine series: 0.681522507 sinφ + 0.111110986 sin3φ − 0.002953041 sin5φ − 0.000012805 sin7φ. Ratios of these coefficients are Q, Q^3, Q^6 with Q = e^{-π/√3} = 0.163034.

TOP OF PAGE (series). Gauss rewrites the numerator as
Zähler = M[sinφ + Q sin3φ − Q^3 sin5φ − Q^6 sin7φ + …], with M = 0.6815225.
He sets v = π√(1/3)/8. Since e^{-8v} = Q and the exponents (2n+1)^2 v − v = 8v·n(n+1)/2, this becomes
Zähler = 0.8549627 [e^{-v} sinφ + e^{-9v} sin3φ − e^{-25v} sin5φ − e^{-49v} sin7φ + …].
Here 0.8549627 = M e^{v}.

Identification (mine). The signs + + − − (period 4) equal (−1)^n·(−1)^{n(n+1)/2}. So the series is Σ(−1)^n q^{n(n+1)} sin(2n+1)φ with q^2 = −e^{-π/√3}, which is θ1(φ,q)/(2q^{1/4}). With q = e^{iπτ} this gives τ = 1/2 + i/(2√3). Then 2 − 1/τ = e^{iπ/3}, so this is the equianharmonic (j = 0) case, the curve with complex multiplication by √−3. This fits the cubic transformation 12x(x²−3x+3)/(x²−3)² on the next page.

The French remark reads: 'En tout cas cela deviendra trop composé' ('in any case this will become too complicated').

COMPUTATION ('Berechnung von s(2/5 ψ)'). The argument is φ = 0.8 R (R = right angle), i.e. φ = 72° = 2π/5. Calculations use 7-place logarithms; Gauss writes log Q^{-1} = log e^{π/√3} = 0.7877229. The multiples are 3φ = 2.4R, 5φ = 4R (so sin5φ = 0 and that term is omitted, my remark), 7φ = 5.6R and 9φ = 7.2R.

(a) Sine series S = sinφ + Q sin3φ − Q^3 sin5φ − Q^6 sin7φ + Q^10 sin9φ.
- Q sin3φ = −0.09582874 (log 9.7692187 − 0.7877229 = 8.9814958).
- −Q^6 sin7φ = −0.000011038 (log 9.7692187 − 4.7263374 = 5.0428813).
- Q^10 sin9φ = −0.000000013 (log 9.9782063 − 7.8772290 = 2.1009773).
- So S = 0.9510565163 − 0.09582874 − 0.000011038 − 0.000000013 = 0.855216725.

(b) Cosine series with the same sign pattern, C = cosφ + Q cos3φ − Q^3 cos5φ − Q^6 cos7φ + Q^10 cos9φ.
- Q cos3φ = −0.131896930 (log 9.1202347).
- −Q^3 = −0.004333425.
- −Q^6 cos7φ = +0.000015192 (log 5.1816202).
- Q^10 cos9φ = +0.000000004 (log 1.6127534).
- So C = 0.3090169944 − 0.131896930 − 0.004333425 + 0.000015192 + 0.000000004 = 0.172801835.

(c) Long division S/C = 4.9491… (digits 4, 9, 4, 9 obtained); it is not used further on this page.

(d) Cosine series with signs + − − + +, i.e. Σ q^{n(n+1)} cos(2n+1)φ, proportional to θ2(φ,q):
C' = 0.3090169944 + 0.131896930 − 0.004333425 − 0.000015192 + 0.000000004 = 0.436565311.

(e) Logarithms: log S = 9.9320762 and log C' = 9.6400492. The difference 0.2920270 is doubled to 0.5840540, and log√3 = 0.2385606 is added, giving 0.8226146.
So s(⅖ψ) = √3 (S/C')^2 = 6.6468301.
This is evidently the value of an equianharmonic elliptic function at 2/5 of the period ψ. On the next page Gauss manipulates this logarithm, √5, and continued fractions, apparently to recognise it as an algebraic (5-division) number.
errors: Line 3 has the exponent written as e^{-25φ}; it should be e^{-25v}. This is a writing slip with no consequence.
log e^{π/√3} is given as 0.7877229, while the true value is 0.7877231. The last-digit discrepancy is negligible at the 7-place precision used.
The final antilog 6.6468301 corresponds to 0.8226146 to the stated precision. Recomputing √3(S/C')^2 directly gives ≈6.64684, which agrees to about 1e-5 (rounding).
No substantive errors otherwise. All additions, subtractions and logarithms check.

results.what: Theta-series (Fourier) expansion of the numerator and denominators of an elliptic function with nome Q = e^{-π/√3} and sign pattern + + − −, i.e. complex nome q^2 = −e^{-π/√3}, τ = 1/2 + i/(2√3), equivalent to e^{iπ/3}
results.modern_name: Jacobi theta functions θ1, θ2 for the equianharmonic (j=0) lattice
results.usually_credited_to: Jacobi (Fundamenta Nova 1829) for theta series; Gauss's unpublished theta work is known from the Nachlass

results.what: Numerical evaluation of the elliptic function value s(2/5 ψ) = √3(θ1/θ2)^2 at φ = 2π/5, about 6.64683, as a 5-division value
results.modern_name: numerical computation of division values of an elliptic function with complex multiplication by √−3
results.usually_credited_to: Abel / Eisenstein (division of lemniscatic and equianharmonic functions); Gauss's work on lemniscatic division known from Disquisitiones §335 and Nachlass

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine numerical work with theta series. Gauss's work on lemniscatic and other singular-modulus elliptic functions and their division values is documented in the Nachlass (Werke III/X). The equianharmonic case and the 5-division computation are a mildly interesting unpublished detail, but the page itself contains only arithmetic.

transcription_corrections: 'e^{-25φ} sin 5φ' is in the manuscript as written, but means e^{-25v}.
'155521651 5' should read 1555216515 (9 × 172801835 in the long division).
'log. s 0,8' and 's 2,4ψ' probably denote the function value at φ = 0.8R, i.e. s(⅖ψ); the symbol before ψ is uncertain.
